evidence.D3.M1: enumerate.py prints the 663 unpinned inventory sites in the seat's 66 production cells. --weights gives each one its consequence weight: 5 for RAISE/GUARD/CMP/CLAMP sites on a hot pattern, down to 1. reach_census.py --lenient reads, for all 663, which traced driver executes the line or reads the file. reach_dead=0: every site is executed by at least one traced driver or read as text by one. 154 sites are executed by exactly one driver, and features.py is the sole executor of 120 of them. select_pool.py ranks the whole universe by weight and then by survivor sweep cost, at most one site per file, and its first 38 lines are the M2 pool (selection_local.txt). C8: the 30-40 target for this round is met by the 38-site pool, not by a sample.
evidence.D3.M2: prescreen.py drives tests/mutation_table.py's own lane over each pooled site: worker clones, null control, killed(), reach_skip. Each site runs against its measured closure minus stress/edge/backtest, plus env_drift.py --all HEAD^1 (= the baseline). The run is from a scratch clone with one local, never-pushed marker commit. Records are prescreen_local.out, prescreen_local.json, and prescreen_local.progress.jsonl (per pair, crash-safe); prescreen_table.py tabulates them. --reach-rows stands in box B3's traced reach rows (same SHA) and runs the baselines untraced here. Tolerated baseline reds at this machine, each one a check that reads no production file: doc_claims (the finder-wall backlog link); entities (5 machinery checks: closure re-derive, PR template, the #1471 window reader x2 because the clone's origin is a local path, and a late-descendant wait); optimality (one claim-closed row, BLAS build). A kill needs more FAILs than these. C2 and C6: dev/audit/rounds/round10/D3/ was stripped from this export by prepare_baseline.sh --strip (the finder wall), so round 10's M25-M36 and its four survivors cannot be re-run here. This round re-pooled from its own universe instead.
evidence.D3.M3: The candidates are prescreen_table.py --survivors, each with its closure, the scripts that ran, and the fact that none killed it. The full GATE_SCOPE=full GOLDEN_MODE=drift gate for the top six survivors belongs to the quiet window (D3.md step 3), never the fan-out, so none of them is a finding yet. C3 and C5 name round 10's survivors and round 10's REPORT.md, which are not in this export (finder wall). They go to the orchestrator's quiet window and record.
evidence.D3.M4: m4.json: for each survivor, the production line, its file, and the check that should have failed.
evidence.D3.M5: m5_table.py (from solves*.out) gives S, A, A/S, and provisional wall/CPU against closures.json seconds for 33 of the 34 scripts. stress.py is quiet-window only. overapprox.py and stale_closure.py cover closure over-approximation (D3-s3-01, -02). repeat_solves.py covers repeat solves (D3-s3-03). C1: this round's M5 has an enumerator (enumerate_m5.py, 34 scripts) and a measured row per script. C4: assertions per solve are measured for 33 of 34, and closure over-approximation is D3-s3-02. C7: the quiet-box gate table is not taken. Wall/CPU are provisional (load1 40-226 here, 2-13 on B3); over-approximation of the 341 s boost_drift_replay closure is measured in D3-s3-02. C9: the kill-overlap matrix needs --overlap (every closure script on every mutant). At about 45 min per features.py run on this box, it was not taken.

non_findings.claim: No unpinned site in the cells is reach-dead. Every one of the 663 is executed by at least one traced gate driver or read as text by one, so no mutant is invisible to the fast suite by construction.
non_findings.value: reach_dead=0 of 663 (executed_by_0=4, all read as text by features.py/entities.py)

non_findings.claim: closures.json's recorded seconds for env_drift.py (1.0 s) and golden.py (1.2 s) understate their real runs by about 150x, but this is disclosed. tests/closure.py's #934 pin keeps the stub-seconds disclosure in the file's _comment, and mutation_table compensates.
non_findings.value: env_drift wall 174 s vs recorded 1.0 s; golden 175 s vs 1.2 s (provisional)

non_findings.claim: arch_score.py's recorded 306 s is its --smoke closure recording by design: the docstring says it is recorded with --smoke, and the full run belongs to CI's arch-instrument job, not the scoped gate (run.sh RUN_PART skip).
non_findings.value: full run cpu 3322 s vs recorded 306 s (provisional, B3)

non_findings.claim: boost_drift_replay.py solves far more than it asserts (789 solves, 46 checks, A/S 0.058), yet the solves are distinct replay steps, not repeats. 786 of 789 inputs are distinct, so no saving exists without changing what the replay covers.
tests/optimality.py and tests/dst_checks.py repeat no solve under the identity key. optimality's 4 deliberate patched re-solves are not counted.
validate.py reports A=0 because it prints ISSUES: bullets rather than ok-lines, which solves.py's assert counter does not read. This is a gap in the harness, not in the suite.
D3-s3-01's stale pairs are not an artefact of B3's Linux strace recorder. Fresh macOS recordings of debug_collect.py and plan_view.py give the same file sets and the same 4 kept pairs.

leads.what: On a loaded box the persistent process_worker child is killed at the parent's shutdown before its atexit runs (repeat_solves.py's original hook lost every worker record on macOS at load1 80). The shutdown path's kill-before-graceful timing under load may deserve a D1 look; it is not measured here.
